issues.description: The problem specification and UML require Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String (the message "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), and the problem/template Main prints that returned value. However, the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and the Goat/Seal implementations print the message and return true. This return-type mismatch between the problem/UML/template and the solution is structural and will confuse students and graders about the expected signature and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String and update Goat and Seal to return the formatted string (e.g. "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing and returning a boolean. Alternatively, if boolean is intended, update the problem statement/UML and template Main to reflect a boolean return and adjust example usage accordingly. Preferably adopt the String return as per the UML and problem description.

issues.description: The conceptual contract for Milkable.messageOnMilk() differs between the problem statement/template and the solution. The problem statement UML and textual requirements specify messageOnMilk() should return a String (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") and the template Main expects to print the returned value (System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())). In the solution, Milkable.messageOnMilk() is declared to return boolean and the implementations print the message and return true. This mismatches the expected return type/behavior and will confuse students mapping the specification to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification and template: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String in the solution interface and update Goat and Seal to return the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (do not print inside the method). Update callers (e.g. Main and any tests) to print the returned String if needed.
